title: Drift database for device-local user models + DAOs + profile erasure
accept: Drift tables exist for exactly the §5 device-local user models (Profile, StoryProgress, WordHelpRecord, TwisterProgress, CollectionState) with the pinned fields and enums (status locked|available|completed; lastHelpLevel none|soundOut|modeled; ageBand three bands); CRUD via DAOs round-trips to the domain types from domain-models.
Max 4 profiles per device enforced at the DAO layer: inserting a 5th profile fails with a typed error (negative test).

WordHelpRecord upsert semantics support the learning signal (§4.3): recordEncounter increments encounterCount; recordHelp increments helpCount and sets lastHelpLevel to the tier reached; a query returns per-word help-rate trajectory over encounters for a profile (test with fixture history).
CollectionState: earning a collectible is idempotent per (profile, collectible) — granting the same collectible twice stores one row (supports Unit 8 first-completion-only rule; test).
StoryProgress: completing a story sets completedAt and increments timesRead; re-reads increment timesRead without duplicating rows (test).
Deleting a profile erases ALL its local data — progress, help records, twister progress, collection — irreversibly; erasure_test verifies a deleted profile leaves zero rows in every table.
All tests run headlessly against an in-memory NativeDatabase (no path_provider, no device).
pinned_design: A-2 pinned: local storage is Drift (SQLite). §5 pinned: all models local-first on device; no server holds user data. Field shapes transcribed exactly from §5 (see domain-models ticket for the authoritative field lists). Unit 10 pinned: up to 4 local profiles; deleting a profile erases all its local data irreversibly. Unit 8 pinned: collectible granted only on first completion (storage must make double-grant impossible). §4.3 pinned: WordHelpRecord powers the help-rate-over-encounters learning signal and the parent pilot view (stories completed + words that needed help, with tier). DAOs expose watch/stream queries (Drift) so Riverpod providers in UI tickets can observe changes; consumers receive domain-model types, not Drift row classes.
notes: Headless testing uses drift's NativeDatabase.memory(), which needs a system libsqlite3 in the container — if absent, orchestrator should add sqlite3 via apt or the sqlite3 dart package's bundled lib. Content models are NOT stored in Drift (packs are file-based, owned by content-delivery). Analytics has its own queue persistence (not this DB) to keep ownership disjoint.
